children: is being sized up by analysts after topping revenue, comparable sales, and profit expectations with its fiscal fourth-quarter report. Sales rose 11.2% to $93.9B during the quarter, and total revenue reached $95.7B, including membership fees. Comparable sales increased 9.4% overall, while digitally enabled comparable sales grew 19.5%. Shares of Costco
slipped 0.6% in premarket trading on Friday.

"Although membership growth is still tepid, COST continues to deliver solid earnings momentum, as a slower pace in paid members is offset by greater engagement & spend per member. In addition, new market openings in the pipeline should drive a re-acceleration in memberships in FY28...COST remains one of the best-positioned retailers in today's consumer environment, supported by structural advantages in supply chain efficiency, value leadership, and scale that we believe will continue to drive market share gains and durable earnings growth."

"Membership metrics remained healthy, with the US/Canada renewal rate improving to 92.3% from 92.2% last quarter, and the worldwide renewal rate increased to 89.8% from 89.7%. At quarter-end there were 84.1 million paid memberships, up 3.8% y/y, while total cardholders increased 3.6% to 150.4 million. Executive memberships grew to 42.3 million and represented 75.6% of sales. Mgmt. noted that targeted digital communications and retention strategies continued to support renewal rate improvements."

"COST delivered another nice quarter, reinforcing its position as one of retail's most durable winners. Strong comps, ~20% digital growth, and membership growth highlight the power of the model. In an environment of elevated gas prices and budget pressures, COST remains a clear beneficiary as shoppers seek savings. However, we do point out that membership growth has decelerated now for ~2 years and just hit its lowest rate since F'4Q17, now at 3.8% as of F'4Q26."
RBC Capital Markets analyst Steven Shemesh

"There were some puts and takes this quarter, but COST's underlying fundamentals remain stable. In our view, the biggest challenge at this juncture remains the multiple. Looking ahead we'll be focused on transaction trends (particularly as tariff refund $s are reinvested) and the trajectory of membership growth. We've updated our model to reflect tariff refunds expected in F1H'27 and tweaked margin, store count, and capex assumptions."

"The story is great, and so are the results. But the market is already pricing in all this bullish narrative and also applying a premium to it. What I'm saying here is that the market already expects that Costco will deliver double digit growth in net income for the next few years, and even considering this, the stock still feels expensive."

title: What analysts are saying about Costco after its earnings report
